environment.description: Same Apollo GraphQL server deployed behind AWS API Gateway HTTP API integration with a usage plan. The API Gateway stage has a route-level throttling configuration with burst limit of 2 and rate limit of 1 request/second specifically on the POST / route (GraphQL endpoint). Additionally, a Lambda@Edge function on the associated CloudFront distribution inspects request bodies for the 'refreshToken' mutation string and applies a stricter token-bucket of 1 request per 30 seconds per source IP, returning 429 before the request reaches API Gateway. The CloudFront behavior has origin request policy that strips and re-adds headers, meaning replayed Authorization headers with tampered tokens trigger the Lambda@Edge evaluation on every attempt. The combination means an attacker cannot perform the iterative token-tampering workflow (sign token with modified role claim, call refreshToken, use new token to call updateRole) within the token's minimum viable window.

config.runtime: Node.js 18 on ECS Fargate behind API Gateway HTTP API
